# dsh-attention-group
**A multi-agent group chat for DSH that decides who is worth waking.**
English · 中文

A durable room for several DSH sessions — plus your own — where a message is written down
first, rou

ted second, and only then allowed to wake anyone. An irrelevant message costs
**zero turns**.
## Why this is not another group chat

Every group chat spends its budget at delivery time: it wakes everyone, and each woken
member then d

iscovers the message was not for them. That is N turns for one message nobody
needed.
This plugin moves the decision *before* the wake. Posting a message returns a routing plan
[代码示例省略，未执行]
or
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Waking is a second, explicit step, and it needs **two** switches to agree (see
Two switches).
Three consequences that are design rules here, not accidents:
- **Creating a room, adding members, reading history, exporting and summarising never wake anybody.*

*
- **A panel message that names nobody wakes nobody** — only NAMING somebody (`@name`, or `@所有人`
wh

ile the room has 「允许 @所有人」 on) **and** the room's 「唤醒」 switch being on makes the panel
wake those pe

ople. Beyond that, the only panel action that starts a turn is 「生成群史摘要」 (also
gated on 「唤醒」 — see Ro

om-history summaries). No name, no event:
a person typing in their own panel is not a reason to run

somebody else's session.
- **Nothing calls another plugin.** Rooms, transcripts, conclusions and exp

orts are plain
files, so this works on a bare DSH and survives this plugin being uninstalled.
## Quick start
### What you need

- DSH **0.2.1-rc.2** (this is the version every interface here was last verified against; it was
fir

st built against 0.2.0-rc.2, re-verified on 0.2.1-rc.1, and re-checked on 0.2.1-rc.2).
- A profile t
o install into. The examples below use `--profile desktop`.

undle patch and its `cordis.patch.yml`.

manageme

nt: it delegates to `pnpm` in the profile directory (run `dsh plugin --profile <name>`
with no subco

mmand and pnpm's own help comes back). What makes the package a *plugin* is that
`package.json` decl
ares `dsh.bundle.patch`.

### Why a long room does not blow up the token budget
"Will a new agent be crushed by a year of chat history?" No, and not by luck:

- **History never enters anyone's context on its own.** A new member writes one member record; not
a

single historical message is sent to it. History is read only when asked for, through
`attention_hi

story` — and that projection is bounded to 200 lines and 2000 characters per line,
and says how many

older lines it left out. The transcript file itself is not touched.
- **A wake-up carries the trigg

er, not the room.** A woken member receives the one message that
matched, the charter (at most 2000

characters) and the self-reflection instruction.
- **Storage grows; context does not.** Transcripts

are append-only JSONL that the plugin never
rewrites, and a line is a few hundred bytes (measured 22

4–494 bytes on real data). Ten thousand
messages is roughly 2–5 MB on disk — and still zero tokens u

l data). Ten thousand
messages is roughly 2–5 MB on disk — and still zero tokens until someone asks.

The same reasoning is why the unread line publishes counts instead of text, and why a summary is a
p
rojection the room keeps rather than a replacement for its history.
## Known limitations
Written down because they are true, not because they are small:
- **DSH version.** Everything here was most recently verified on **DSH 0.2.1-rc.2** (and before that
re-checked after the 0.2.0-rc.2 → 0.2.1-rc.1 upgrade): every service this plugin reads is still pre

sent and
the session format is still v4. That check was done by reading the running runtime, not by

assuming — `agents.resume` still takes `{resumeSessionId, agentOptions, setup}`, the message
`source

.kind` rule still accepts any producer-owned kind except the retired `"plugin"`, and the
tool regist

ry still compiles the inline `required: true` parameter dialect into a standard JSON
Schema (confirm

ed through the runtime's own tool-inspection provider). The interface shape is
only claimed for 0.2.

x; a minor DSH release can still move a service it reads.
- **Host-side changes need a restart.** A

restart is required after installing or changing
host code; a plugin-panel toggle does not re-import

the module (measured: a new tool stayed
`unknown tool`). The browser half is served as a **disk sna

pshot** — its changes need a
page reload, and a reload can arrive before the host process is restart

ed, which is why the
panel degrades gracefully instead of failing.
- **Reasoning effort reaches a li

ve session only if you ask, and only on web-app deployments.**
A session that is **stored** gets the

room's effort for free when it is woken. A session that
is **live** can also be changed in place —

`sessionController.selectModel` exists and does
work — but it is behind a per-room switch, `liveEffo

rt`, which is **off by default**, because
that same call also saves the selection as the deployment

default model. It takes effect from
the session's **next step**, not on a request already in flight.

And `sessionController` is
mounted by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`: a headless deployment does not ha

ve it, in which case
the panel says so rather than pretending the switch works.
(`unverified`: the c

all is verified in the sources and covered by tests against a stand-in
service; it has not yet been

exercised against a real live session on this machine.)
